safi-cedvel:1-3.t:
* I'rab:
(يكن) is a defective imperfect, jussive, and it was vowelled with kasra because of the meeting of two quiescents (الذين) is a relative, the ism of يكن, in the position of nominative (من أهل) is attached to a ḥāl from the agent of كفروا (حتّى) is a particle of limit and of governing the genitive (تأتيهم) is an imperfect, accusative by an implied أن after حتّى..
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن تأتيهم..) is in the position of genitive by (حتّى), attached to (منفكّين) [Note: if (منفكّين) is an active participle of the defective verb (ما انفكّ), then the attachment is to an implied khabar, i.e.: "they continue to persist in their disbelief until the clear proof comes to them".].
Clause: «لم يكن الذين ... » has no grammatical position; it is an opening clause.
And the clause: «كفروا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
And the clause: «تأتيهم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied particle-relative (أن).
Verses 2-3: (رسول) is a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) for البيّنة [Note: or a badal muṭābiq (congruent substitute) by way of exaggeration.. or it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ.], (من الله) is attached to a naʿt of (رسول) [Note: or attached to رسول on the basis that it is derived.], (فيها) is attached to a fronted khabar for the mubtadaʾ (كتب).
And the clause: «يتلو ... » is in the position of nominative, a naʿt of رسول [Note: or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from رسول because it has been specified by the description.].
And the clause: «فيها كتب ... » is in the position of accusative, a naʿt of (صحفا).

* Morphology:
(منفكّين): an active participle from the quinqueliteral انفكّ, plural of منفكّ; its pattern is منفعل, with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn, and its ʿayn and lām come from one letter.

safi-cedvel:4-5.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is a conjunction (ما) is negating (إلّا) is for restriction (من بعد) is attached to (تفرّق), (ما) is a maṣdar particle..
And the interpreted maṣdar (ما جاءتهم البيّنة) is in the position of genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
Clause: «ما تفرّق الذين ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the opening clause.
And the clause: «أوتوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
And the clause: «جاءتهم البيّنة» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-relative (ما).
Verse 5: (الواو) is a conjunction in the first three places, and resumptive in the fourth (ما) is negating, and the (الواو) in (أمروا) is the nāʾib fāʿil (إلّا) is for restriction (اللام) is for causation (يعبدوا) is an accusative imperfect by an implied أن after the lām (مخلصين) is an accusative ḥāl from the agent of يعبدوا (له) is attached to (مخلصين) (الدين) is the mafʿūl bihi of the active participle مخلصين (حنفاء) is a second accusative ḥāl..
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن يعبدوا) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to (أمروا) [Note: i.e. they were not commanded with what they were commanded except for the sake of worship.].
(يقيموا) is an accusative imperfect conjoined to (يعبدوا), and likewise (يؤتوا) ..
And the clause: «ما أمروا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause ما تفرّق الذين [Note: it is possible that the clause is circumstantial, indicating the ugliness of what they did, i.e.: they split after the coming of the clear proof, while they had been commanded to worship Allah.]..
And the clause: «يعبدوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied particle-relative (أن).
And the clause: «يقيموا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause يعبدوا.
And the clause: «يؤتوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause يقيموا.
And the clause: «ذلك دين ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.

safi-cedvel:6-6.t:
* I'rab:
(من أهل) is attached to a ḥāl from the agent of كفروا (في نار) is attached to an omitted khabar of inna (خالدين) is an accusative ḥāl from the latent pronoun in the khabar of inna (فيها) is attached to (خالدين) (هم) is a separation pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) «1» ..
Clause: «إنّ الذين كفروا ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «كفروا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
And the clause: «أولئك ... شر البريّة» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption — or causal [Note: or in the position of nominative, a second khabar of (إنّ).]

* Morphology:
(البريّة): a collective noun meaning "creation", derived from البري, which is dust; the pattern of البريّة is فعيلة in the sense of مفعولة; it is possible that البريّة is a lightened form of the hamzated one, its origin being البريئة, from برأ الله الخلق, i.e. He originated it..

safi-cedvel:7-8.t:
* I'rab:
(هم) is a separation pronoun «3», (عند) is an accusative adverbial attached to a ḥāl from جنّات [Note: it is possible that it is attached to (جزاؤهم) or to a ḥāl from it.] (من تحتها) is attached to (تجري) [Note: or attached to a ḥāl from الأنهار.], with omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "from beneath its trees.. or its palaces" (خالدين) is an accusative ḥāl [Note: the governing element of the ḥāl is omitted, i.e. "their entering it"; and it is not valid for the governing element to be (جزاؤهم), so that the maṣdar and its dependent not be separated by a foreign element..], (أبدا) is an accusative adverb of time attached to (خالدين), (عنهم) is attached to (رضي), (عنه) is attached to (رضوا), and the indication in (ذلك) is to the abiding in Paradise (لمن) is attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (ذلك) ..
Clause: «إنّ الذين آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
And the clause: «عملوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the ṣila clause.
And the clause: «أولئك ... خير البريّة» is in the position of nominative, the khabar of inna.
And the clause: «جزاؤهم ... جنّات» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
And the clause: «تجري ... » is in the position of accusative, a ḥāl from جنّات [Note: (جنّات) is annexed to عدن — a proper noun — so it acquired definiteness, or — a generic noun — so it acquired specification by annexation.].
And the clause: «رضي الله ... » has no grammatical position; it is a resumptive of supplication [Note: it is possible that it is a second khabar of (إنّ), and the clause جزاؤهم ... جنّات is parenthetical.].
And the clause: «رضوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause رضي الله.
And the clause: «ذلك لمن خشي ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
And the clause: «خشي ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (من).

* Benefits:
- The pleasure of the Lord and the pleasure of the servant:
The scholars said: Pleasure (riḍā) is divided into two kinds: pleasure in Him (riḍā bihi), and pleasure with Him (riḍā ʿanhu). Pleasure in Him is that He be Lord and Disposer; pleasure with Him is in what He decrees and disposes. Al-Sarī said: "If you are not pleased with Allah, how do you ask Him to be pleased with you?" It is also said: He was pleased with their deeds, and they were pleased with Him for what He gave them of good and honour.
On the authority of Anas ibn Mālik, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet ﷺ said to Ubayy ibn Kaʿb: "Allah has commanded me to recite to you (لم يكن)." He said: "And He named me?" He said: "Yes." So he wept.
In al-Bukhārī's report, the Prophet ﷺ said to Ubayy ibn Kaʿb: "Allah has commanded me to have you recite the Qur'an." He said: "Did Allah name me to you?" He said: "Yes." He said: "And I was mentioned before the Lord of the worlds?" He said: "Yes." He said:
and his eyes shed tears.
As for Ubayy's weeping, he wept out of joy or out of belittling himself. As for singling out this sūra for the recitation, it is, despite its brevity, comprehensive of fundamentals, principles and great matters. As for the wisdom in the command to the Prophet ﷺ to recite to Ubayy, it is that Ubayy learn the recitation from his own words ﷺ, and master the prescribed style of metre and measure; so his recitation to Ubayy was for Ubayy to learn from him, not for him to learn from Ubayy. It is also said: he recited to Ubayy only so that others would learn humility and good manners, and that a noble man of high rank should not disdain to learn the Qur'an from one beneath him. In it also is a notice of Ubayy's excellence, and an urging to take from him and to put him forward in that. So he was after the Prophet ﷺ a head and imam in recitation and other things, and was one of the scholars among the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them all.
